candidates: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by(...) without handling the no-row case, which will raise and return a 500 when the current user has no topic_users record for that topic

TopicsController#unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change() so notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at aren't set for a user-initiated notification_level change, allowing update_last_read auto-tracking to later overwrite the user's choice

The unsubscribe route is defined as GET but the controller action mutates TopicUser.notification_level and saves it, making it vulnerable to CSRF via link/image injection since no CSRF token is required on GET requests
The GET unsubscribe endpoint will be triggered unintentionally by email client link prefetchers, silently changing users' notification settings
